name: Morning dress

card.summary: Morning dress is the formal Western daytime outfit of morning coat, waistcoat and striped trousers, whose long cutaway lines and tailoring give a tall, polished silhouette.
card.note: Worn mainly at weddings and events like Royal Ascot, where dress codes are specified by organisers.

quick.overview:
Morning dress is the traditional formal daytime dress code: a single-breasted morning coat with curved tails, a waistcoat, striped or checked trousers, a white shirt, and polished black shoes. Its appearance payoff is a structured, elongated look that signals formality.

It developed from riding coats in the 19th century and replaced the frock coat as standard daytime full dress in the Edwardian era. Today it is seen at British and Commonwealth weddings, Royal Ascot, and some official occasions.
quick.how: Men wear the coat and waistcoat (matching or contrasting), striped trousers with braces and no turn-ups, a white double-cuff shirt with tie or cravat, black Oxford shoes, and optionally a top hat, gloves and boutonniere. Variants include a matching morning suit and all-grey morning grey.
quick.risks: There are no health risks. Practical issues are etiquette: Royal Ascot banned cravats in 2012 and bow ties in 2019 in the Royal Enclosure, and the code is not for events starting after 18:00.

lead: Morning dress is the formal Western daytime dress code, worn by men in a morning coat, waistcoat and striped or checked trousers.[2] The coat is single-breasted with peaked lapels and knee-length cutaway tails, traditionally in black or Oxford grey.[2]
For looks, it is a structured outfit: the long coat and tailored trousers create a lengthened line, and the matching ensemble is considered a hallmark of well-dressed formal wear.[2]

The name comes from gentlemen riding in the morning in cutaway coats; the dress began as casual half dress and became acceptable for formal occasions, and by the Edwardian era it replaced the frock coat as standard daytime full dress.[2][1]

chain: Structured coat with cutaway tails and striped trousers
angle.text: The outfit gives a long, tailored line and a coordinated formal look used at weddings and races.

infobox: Morning coat, waistcoat, striped trousers, white shirt, black shoes

paras: The waistcoat matches the coat for the most formal look, though dove grey, buff or camel contrasts are common at weddings and races. Trousers are striped or black-and-white checked, worn with braces, no turn-ups and no belt.[2]
The shirt is white with double cuffs and a turndown collar; shoes are highly polished black Oxfords. Accessories include top hat, gloves, pocket square, cane or umbrella and optional spats.[2]

Fashion plates of 1848 show it as an alternative to the frock coat; in the Edwardian era it became standard daytime full dress.[2] The Kennedy inauguration in 1961 was the last to use it for that ceremony.[2]

Variants include morning suit (matching cloth), morning grey, and an all-black version for court and funerals. Occasions include weddings, Royal Ascot, Epsom Derby, and Harvard Commencement; per Debrett's it is not for events after 18:00.[2]
Royal Ascot banned cravats in 2012 and bow ties in 2019 in the Royal Enclosure.[2]
